A1.justification: Both PDFs describe On the Guidance of Flow Matching. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated limitations and renumbered appendix material.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic sampling, D4RL planning, and CelebA-HQ image inverse experiments in Section 4, with additional results and analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments in Section 4 and Appendix B, and adds a CFM versus OT-CFM vector-field analysis in Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 adds gMC-IS, an importance-sampling variant using an alternative proposal distribution and density-ratio weights, with approximately guided sampling suggested for constructing the proposal. Existing guidance methods and training losses remain unchanged; empirical investigation of this variant is explicitly deferred.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the synthetic distribution transports, nine D4RL locomotion tasks, and CelebA-HQ inpainting, super-resolution, and deblurring. The new vector-field diagnostic uses the existing image domain without establishing additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in the corresponding experiments, including CEG for synthetic sampling, BC and Diffuser for planning, and ΠGDM for image restoration. The new diagnostic compares existing CFM and OT-CFM backbones without introducing another guidance comparator.

E3.justification: New Table 3 introduces a diagnostic measuring relative L2 differences between CFM and OT-CFM vector fields at flow times 0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 0.95. Previously stated benchmark splits, corruption settings, metrics, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds an empirical examination of the P≈1 approximation through vector-field differences on CelebA images. Existing Monte Carlo sample-count sensitivity, epsilon ablation, return-distribution analyses, and image case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five seeded planning runs and retain the same standard deviations and existing uncertainty displays. New Table 3 adds ±-formatted results but specifies no new repeated-run count or statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports five relative L2 results, including 0.0382±0.0076 at t=0.05, 0.0271±0.0032 at t=0.5, and 0.0717±0.0096 at t=0.95. All pre-existing benchmark tables, ablation values, and figure results are unchanged after matching renumbering.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds mathematical reasoning about source-distribution consistency under P≈1. The error-bound summary gains an energy-dependent denominator in v3 A.9, although its power still differs from the retained displayed bound. A.1 also introduces an incorrect J=p(y|x) prescription beside the correct negative-log definition. Core theorems and proofs otherwise remain largely unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the unified guidance framework, asymptotically exact Monte Carlo guidance, training-based guidance, and recovery of classical methods. Explicitly naming energy guidance clarifies the scope already established in v2 rather than changing the central contribution.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.3 explains approximation error through source-distribution or vector-field mismatch, discusses slowly varying energies under strong coupling, and identifies difficulties when both coupling and energy variation are strong. It interprets Table 3 as support for P≈1. Most existing limitations are retained and moved into Section 5.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly discloses trying CFM and OT-CFM guidance fields with each pretrained backbone and reporting the best result. This documents selection for retained results without establishing a changed experiment. Hardware, training details, and the code destination remain unchanged; v2's linked 'here' already points to the repository printed in v3.

R1.justification: v3 adds Andrae et al. (2025) and Hiranaka et al. (2025), removes Zhang et al. (2023), and changes the training-loss positioning from classifier-free to classifier guidance. The named replacements for Anonymous (2025a–d) correspond to the same previously cited works.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify energy guidance, approximation arguments, and the Jacobian discussion. Limitations move from Appendix B to main Section 5, experimental details become Appendix B, and author ordering, equal-contribution information, and an impact statement change. Most wording and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the compact vector-field comparison Table 3 and reflows existing figures and tables around the expanded text. Figures 1–7 retain their content, and v2 Tables 3–5 become v3 Tables 4–6 without redesign. Conference information also changes the first-page layout.

improvement.justification: The expanded coupling discussion, targeted diagnostic, corrected classifier-guidance positioning, and disclosed planning selection modestly improve clarity and transparency. These gains are limited: Table 3 measures unguided-field similarity rather than guidance accuracy, gMC-IS remains untested, and new Appendix A.1 prose incorrectly sets J=p(y|x) despite the correct negative-log derivation. The core evidence and unresolved scalability limitations remain unchanged.
